title: 1F916 /api/proof response
description: RFC 6962 inclusion proof for one sealed row against the first checkpoint that covers it. A verifier folds SHA-256(0x00 || hash-hex-as-utf8) up the proof path and the result must equal checkpoint.root; with the checkpoint signature and a witness copy that places the event in the log by checkpoint time, on math alone. log is exactly the source LOGS tuple (identity_events | ledger). A 200 never carries a null event.hash: rows without a chain hash 409 as predates-sealing rather than proving a gap as an empty proof. The how_to_verify field is server-authored prose: pin presence and stringness, never the wording. Cross-field (proof length vs tree_size, leaf_index < tree_size) is stated here because the subset validator cannot compare two fields; the live probes on both logs are the runtime check.

log.description: Mirrors src/checkpoint.ts LOGS exactly. Any other value is a 400, not a 200.

proof.description: RFC 6962 §2.1.1 sibling hashes, lowercase 64-hex, from leaf toward root. Empty is a legitimate tree-of-one; do not require minItems.

how_to_verify.description: Server-authored verification recipe. Presence is the contract; wording is not pinned.

registry_key_history.description: The registry's signing keys by epoch, with the rotation statements that link them, as GET /api/checkpoint serves it (schemas/checkpoint.json registry_key_history). Served so this file alone tells a verifier which key checks each head it carries. Absent on a deployment with no registry key configured.

final_consistency.description: Present when the covering checkpoint was signed by a registry key since retired and is smaller than that key's committed final head for this log (registry_key_history rotation.final_heads): the RFC 6962 consistency proof from this checkpoint to that final head. verify.mjs accepts such a head only with it.

id.description: Row id in the named log

hash.description: The sealed row hash (lowercase hex). A 200 never serves null: unsealed rows 409.

leaf_index.description: 0-based index into the sealed-hash leaf set (not the raw row id; unsealed prefix rows are skipped). 0 is a real index (first sealed ledger row).

tree_size.description: Sealed leaves covered by this checkpoint; the inclusion query picks the smallest tree_size >= leaf_index+1

created_at.description: Ms epoch when this checkpoint was signed
